title: What's Inside a Pencil?

creative.hook: Take apart the most ordinary object a child owns, one layer at a time, and find eight surprises hiding inside it.
creative.learningGoal: Know what a pencil is really made of, how it is built from flat wood, and what happens when you write and erase.
creative.signatureMoment: The final answer unspools one pencil line back and forth across the screen until the whole panel is filled.

script.pencil_005-answer: Six flat sides stop a pencil rolling off your desk. And one wooden sandwich makes six to nine pencils.
script.pencil_006-answer: To boast about their graphite. The story goes that in eighteen eighty-nine, yellow showed that a pencil's graphite came from China.
script.pencil_009-answer: Flakes of graphite! It is stacked sheets that slide apart, and a pencil can leave one just an atom thick. That is graphene.
script.pencil_010-answer: About forty-five thousand words — a whole book from one little stick! And the famous thirty-five mile line? Too good to be true.

questions.question: A pencil's lead is not lead at all. So what is it?
questions.explanation: Pencils have never held lead. The dark core is graphite mixed with clay.

visual.alt: A close-up of a sharpened pencil point, showing the dark graphite core writing on paper
visual.answerHint: Never lead, not once in four hundred years

questions.question: True or false: more clay makes a pencil draw darker.
questions.explanation: More clay makes it harder and lighter — that is H. More graphite makes it darker — that is B.

visual.alt: A cutaway of the pencil showing the graphite and clay core running inside the wood
visual.answerHint: More clay is harder, more graphite is darker

questions.question: The core is not drilled in. Put the real steps in order.
questions.answer: groove the wood, lay in the core, glue, then slice
questions.explanation: A pencil is built like a sandwich, and one sandwich is cut into six to nine pencils.

visual.alt: Two flat pieces of wood with a groove, the core laid inside, glued together and cut into pencils

questions.question: Which wood sharpens without splintering, so most pencils are made of it?
questions.explanation: Cedar is soft enough to sharpen cleanly, and it does not warp.

visual.alt: A close-up of the sharpened cedar cone with wood shavings curling away

questions.question: Why do most pencils have six flat sides?
questions.explanation: Six flat sides stop a pencil rolling off your desk, and one wooden sandwich makes six to nine of them.

visual.alt: A six-sided pencil end resting still on a desk while a round one rolls over the edge

questions.question: Why were the fanciest old pencils painted bright yellow?
options: To be easy to find at night
questions.explanation: The story goes that an 1889 show pencil wore royal yellow to boast that its graphite came from China. Other makers copied it.

visual.alt: A close-up of the painted barrel, showing coat after coat of yellow paint
visual.answerHint: Yellow was a boast about Chinese graphite

questions.question: Which part of a pencil am I?
clues: I am a little metal band
I am crimped tight at one end
Without me the eraser would fall off
questions.explanation: The little metal band is clamped around the eraser to hold it on.

visual.alt: A close-up of the crimped metal band that clamps the eraser to the wood

questions.question: True or false: an eraser scrubs your mark into dust.
questions.explanation: It mostly lifts. Graphite sticks to rubber better than to paper, so the mark leaves with the crumbs.

visual.alt: A close-up of the eraser rubbing a pencil mark away and lifting it into the crumbs

questions.question: When you write, what leaves the pencil and stays on the paper?
questions.explanation: Graphite is stacked sheets that slide apart. A pencil can leave one just an atom thick: that is graphene, which won a Nobel Prize.

visual.alt: Stacked sheets of graphite with the top sheet sliding off onto the paper below

questions.question: Roughly how many words can one pencil write?
questions.explanation: About 45,000 words: a whole book from one little stick. People also say a pencil draws a line 35 miles long, but when a mathematician checked the sums, it came out far shorter.

visual.alt: A single pencil line unspooling back and forth across the panel
visual.answerHint: Enough words to fill a book
